messages.subject: Different results in GGIR depending on whether a bin file is processed alone or in a bunch
parts:
Dear all,

There is probably an easy answer to my question but I cannot seem to
figure it out. I am processing a set of GeneActiv data (87.5 Hz, 7
days + previous and following night) and it looks like I am getting
different results depending on whether the file was processed on its
own (i.e., being the only file in the folder) or in a bunch (i.e.,
together with other files from the same study, currently 65).

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Different results in GGIR depending on whether a bin file is processed alone or in a bunch
parts:
Thanks Kenn for your detailed post,

I am struggling to reproduce the issue with an Axivity 50 Hertz .cwa and a GENEActiv 100 Hertz .bin recording, regardless of whether I rely on GENEAread or on GGIRread (controlled by argument loadGENEActiv). For this test I used Windows, but I can try again in Ubuntu in upcoming days.

1. To aid the investigation it would be good to know in which GGIR part the differences first appear. Are the snapshots of the time series you shared from GGIR part 1 or 2?

2. What OS are you using?

3. Do you get the same result if you reprocess the files in a new output folder while simplifying your GGIR call to only the basic argument:
GGIR::GGIR(datadir = indir, outputdir = "results", desiredtz = "Europe/Tallinn", studyname = "AUU")? If yes, then that may allow us to track down which of the input arguments that are left out and corresponding functions is causing the difference.

4. Could it be that memory per process is unusually low on your machine that this somehow kills or interrupts the parallel jobs? I have to say that GGIR does not monitor that in high detail but assumes that process has roughly 2 GB available (e.g. 16 GB RAM on 8 core laptop). If this would be an issue then maybe test chunksize = 0.4 which reduce the memory needs of GGIR per process. If this solves the difference then that would indicate that GGIR needs to be improved to monitor available memory and data loss in more detail.

On a side note: Function GGIR::g.shell.GGIR has become a wrapper around function GGIR::GGIR, so you can use either of them but we introduced the latter as it is easier to pronounce and type. This should play no role in the issue, but just wanted to highlight it.

Best regards,

Vincent

parts:
Hi Vincent,

First of all, many thanks for a quick response! It did indeed help me locate the problem, which seems to be related to how file names are stored in g.part1, rather than the processing itself.

I am using a set of self-made functions (packaged, as for now, mostly for my own use, as https://github.com/lebatsnok/afterGGIR) to facilitate my workflow with GGIR. One of these functions reads in the .RData files in GGIR output, among these the files in "results/output_XYZ/meta/basic", and uses the variable called filename_dir as a starting point to find out the subject ID (coded into the file name). It appears (if I'm not mistaken) that this variable is occasionally wrong if there are many files in the source folder.

The following code demonstrates what I think to be a bug (probably irrelevant  to most users, though):

get.id.from.file <- function(fn) sub("Subject Code:", "", readLines(fn, 39, skipNul=TRUE)[39])
get.id.from.ggir.results <- function(fn) Load(paste0("results/output_", dirname(fn), "/meta/basic/meta_", basename(fn), ".RData"))$filename_dir
# `Load` (source at the end of this email or in lebatsnok/afterGGIR) loads everything from an
# Rdata file into a temporary environment, converts this into a list and returns this list
# (leaving the global environment unchanged!)

processed_files <- paste0("bin/", sub(".RData$", "", sub("meta_", "", dir("results/output_bin/meta/basic"))))

id1 <- sapply(processed_files, get.id.from.file)                                              
id2 <- sapply(processed_files, get.id.from.ggir.results)                                              
id3 <- sapply(strsplit(basename(id2), "_"), head, 1)

df <- data.frame(filename = processed_files, bin.id = id1, ggir.id = id3, ggir.fn = id2)
rownames(df) <- NULL

openxlsx::write.xlsx(df, "df.xlsx") ## the result is attached

In this table, the participant's ID code appears in three columns:

1) File name (column A)
2) "Subject Code:" - 39th row in bin file (column B, always identical to the ID in column A)
3) "ggir.fn" -  the filename_dir variable from .RData file in meta/basic directory (column D)
4) "ggir.id" - the ID component extracted from the filename (as recorded in filename_dir variable, column C)

In the original data folder, there are 2 bin files that did not produce output, one of them (ID=1750) containing no data (2KB, 64 header rows in the bin file, probably something happened during download, which we haven't yet checked) - and the discrepancy appears right after that file. That is, for the first 35 files, file name in `filename_dir` in meta/basic/*.RData is correct, and for the remaining files, it refers to the preceding file.

I believe I can now solve my problem (using the actual filename instead  of filename_dir variable) but the part in GGIR part 1 code that produces filename_dir may be worth checking.

Best regards,
Kenn


Load <- function (file, to.list = TRUE, Unlist = TRUE, spray = FALSE, 
    delete.parent = FALSE, Attach = FALSE) 
{
    attachYN <- (is.logical(Attach) & isTRUE(Attach)) | is.character(Attach)
    if (attachYN) {
        attachNAME <- if (is.logical(Attach)) 
            date()
        else Attach[1]
    }
    NE <- if (spray) 
        .GlobalEnv
    else if (attachYN) 
        attach(NULL, name = attachNAME)
    else new.env()
    load(file, NE)
    if (attachYN) 
        return(invisible(NULL))
    if (to.list) {
        NE <- as.list(NE)
        if (Unlist & length(NE) == 1) 
            NE <- NE[[1]]
    }
    if (delete.parent) 
        parent.env(NE) <- emptyenv()
    NE
}

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Different results in GGIR depending on whether a bin file is processed alone or in a bunch
parts:
Hi Kenn,

Thanks for sharing your observation. I think I see where the problem comes from. Object filename_dir is indeed incorrect but because it is never used in GGIR nobody every noticed the mistake. Instead GGIR uses the name of the underlying accelerometer file inside the name of the RData file, and that is what GGIR across GGIR to keep track of the different files. This process should be unaffected by parallel versus non-parallel processing.

Conclusions/Action points:
  • Do not trust filename_dir. Instead use the filename incorreported in the name of the RData file.
  • We will have to fix or deprecate object filename_dir. I have created an issue for this: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/721#issuecomment-1359770041
  • It looks like this segment of the GGIR code could benefit from some cleaning up work more generally as it seems old and not clearly written. 

Best regards,

Vincent

Hi Vincent,

First of all, many thanks for a quick response! It did indeed help me locate the problem, which seems to be related to how file names are stored in g.part1, rather than the processing itself.

I am using a set of self-made functions (packaged, as for now, mostly for my own use, as https://github.com/lebatsnok/afterGGIR) to facilitate my workflow with GGIR. One of these functions reads in the .RData files in GGIR output, among these the files in "results/output_XYZ/meta/basic", and uses the variable called filename_dir as a starting point to find out the subject ID (coded into the file name). It appears (if I'm not mistaken) that this variable is occasionally wrong if there are many files in the source folder.

The following code demonstrates what I think to be a bug (probably irrelevant to most users, though):

get.id.from.file <- function(fn) sub("Subject Code:", "", readLines(fn, 39, skipNul=TRUE)[39])
get.id.from.ggir.results <- function(fn) Load(paste0("results/output_", dirname(fn), "/meta/basic/meta_", basename(fn), ".RData"))$filename_dir
# `Load` (source at the end of this email or in lebatsnok/afterGGIR) loads everything from an
# Rdata file into a temporary environment, converts this into a list and returns this list
# (leaving the global environment unchanged!)

id1 <- sapply(processed_files, get.id.from.file)
id2 <- sapply(processed_files, get.id.from.ggir.results)
id3 <- sapply(strsplit(basename(id2), "_"), head, 1)

Load <- function (file, to.list = TRUE, Unlist = TRUE, spray = FALSE,
    delete.parent = FALSE, Attach = FALSE)
{
    attachYN <- (is.logical(Attach) & isTRUE(Attach)) | is.character(Attach)
    if (attachYN) {
        attachNAME <- if (is.logical(Attach))
            date()
        else Attach[1]
    }
    NE <- if (spray)
        .GlobalEnv
    else if (attachYN)
        attach(NULL, name = attachNAME)
    else new.env()
    load(file, NE)
    if (attachYN)
        return(invisible(NULL))
    if (to.list) {
        NE <- as.list(NE)
        if (Unlist & length(NE) == 1)
            NE <- NE[[1]]
    }
    if (delete.parent)
        parent.env(NE) <- emptyenv()
    NE
}

Thanks Kenn for your detailed post,

I am struggling to reproduce the issue with an Axivity 50 Hertz .cwa and a GENEActiv 100 Hertz .bin recording, regardless of whether I rely on GENEAread or on GGIRread (controlled by argument loadGENEActiv). For this test I used Windows, but I can try again in Ubuntu in upcoming days.

1. To aid the investigation it would be good to know in which GGIR part the differences first appear. Are the snapshots of the time series you shared from GGIR part 1 or 2?

2. What OS are you using?

3. Do you get the same result if you reprocess the files in a new output folder while simplifying your GGIR call to only the basic argument:
GGIR::GGIR(datadir = indir, outputdir = "results", desiredtz = "Europe/Tallinn", studyname = "AUU")? If yes, then that may allow us to track down which of the input arguments that are left out and corresponding functions is causing the difference.

4. Could it be that memory per process is unusually low on your machine that this somehow kills or interrupts the parallel jobs? I have to say that GGIR does not monitor that in high detail but assumes that process has roughly 2 GB available (e.g. 16 GB RAM on 8 core laptop). If this would be an issue then maybe test chunksize = 0.4 which reduce the memory needs of GGIR per process. If this solves the difference then that would indicate that GGIR needs to be improved to monitor available memory and data loss in more detail.

On a side note: Function GGIR::g.shell.GGIR has become a wrapper around function GGIR::GGIR, so you can use either of them but we introduced the latter as it is easier to pronounce and type. This should play no role in the issue, but just wanted to highlight it.

Best regards,

Vincent
